summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, colorectal cancer, chronic kidney disease, and malnutrition, was admitted with shortness of breath and cough due to left lower lobe pneumonia, leading to sepsis and acute hypoxic respiratory failure. He was intubated and treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to meropenem after bronchoscopy identified pseudomonas aeruginosa. He was extubated but re-intubated due to mucus plugging and an aspirated tablet, prompting a tracheostomy for airway management and pulmonary rehabilitation. His septic shock resolved, kidney function improved, and he was weaned to a trach mask. Nutrition was supported with enteral and parenteral feeding due to high gastric residuals. He was discharged to an extended care facility on IV meropenem, with plans for physical therapy and gradual tracheostomy decannulation.
